items.summary: 전남광주 서구의 한 도로에서 70대 여성이 운전하던 승용차에 70대 보행자가 치여 숨지는 사고가 발생했다.광주 서부경찰서는 27일 교통사고처리특례법위반(치사) 혐의로 70대 여성을 입건해 조사 중이라고 밝혔다.이 여성은 이날 오전 4시 56분경 전남광주 서구 양동 아파트 인근 단일 도로에서 그랜저 승용차를 몰다 횡단보도에 있던 70대 노인을 친 혐의를 받고 있다.이 사고로 횡단보도를 건너던 노인이 크게 다쳐 병원으로 옮겨졌으나 결국 숨졌다.사고 당시 운전자는 음주 상태나 무면허 운전은 아니었던 것으로 조사됐다.경찰은 주변 폐쇄회로(CC)TV 영상 및 차량 블랙박스 등을 확보해 정확한 사고 경위를 조사하고 있다.

items.title: 먹는 약부터 근육 지키는 약까지…비만약 ‘3위 전쟁’ 불붙었다
items.summary: 글로벌 비만치료제 시장을 장악한 일라이 릴리와 노보 노디스크의 뒤를 이을 3위 경쟁이 달아오르고 있다. 로슈와 화이자, 암젠, 아스트라제네카 등 글로벌 빅파마들이 임상 3상 진입과 인수합병(M&A), 기술도입을 거치며 저마다의 전략을 구체화하면서다.특히 로슈가 한미약품의 차세대 비만 신약 후보물질까지 품으면서 경쟁에 불을 붙였다. 기존 GLP-1 계열의 체중 감량 효과만을 좇던 경쟁은 경구제와 장기지속형, 아밀린, 근육 보존 등으로 빠르게 확장되고 있다.27일 업계에 따르면 로슈그룹 제넨텍은 지난 24일 한미약품(128940)과 ‘HM17321’의 한국을 제외한 전 세계 개발·제조·상업화 독점권을 확보하는 최대 23억달러(약 3조 5000억 원) 규모 계약을 체결했다.HM17321은 기존 인크레틴 계열과 다른 UCN2(우로코르틴-2) 유사체로, 체지방을 줄이면서 제지방과 근육을 보존·증가시키는 것을 목표로 개발되고 있다.현재 시장은 릴리와 노보의 양강 구도가 뚜렷하다.

articles.title: 네팔 ‘돌발 홍수’에 400명 실종… 한국인 9명 포함

articles.snippet: 웃기지도 않는 아재개그인 줄 알았다. “검사 출신인 더불어민주당 박균택 이건태 의원 등이 정성호 법무부 장관 후임에 거론되고 있다”는 지난주 동아일보 기사를 봤을 때다. 가볍게 넘길 일이 아닌 것 같다. 김민석 국무총리 후임으로 정성호 법무부 장관과 강훈식 대통령비서실장, ‘여성 총리 카드’로 한성숙 중소벤처기업부 장관이 거론된다는 보도가 나온 지 사흘도 안 돼 한성숙이 총리로 지명됐다. 그리고는 야당이 반대하든 말든 여당끼리 임명동의안을 처리해 대통령 뜻을 받들었다. 장난처럼 들리던 ‘대장동 변호인’ 박균택 이건태의 법무장관 하마평이 사라지지 않는 게 심상찮다. 인사권이 대통령 고유권한인 줄 알고 가만히 있으면, 국민을 가마니로 안다. 이 대통령은 말로는 “외연확장” 주장하면서 새 총리도 내각 아니면 비서실에서 찾다 제일 무게감 적은 한성숙을 찍었다. 이번엔 다른 장관도 아닌 법무장관을 ‘여의도 로펌’에서 찾는 것을 설마 싶어 가만 두고 볼 순 없다.● ‘공소취소’

articles.snippet: One autumn day in 2023 I bathed in the luminous glow of this utterly authentic star – and while she did have one weak spot, her life and music will speak for themselves Celebrity tributes pour in for Dolly Parton Dolly Parton’s 10 best deep cuts Alexis Petridis on Dolly Parton’s peerless career The great privilege of my kind of journalism is to get the chance to meet extraordinary people – some famous, many not – and very occasionally that person is beyond extraordinary. Dolly Parton, you may not be surprised to learn, was one of them. I’ve only come across it a handful of times. It has nothing to do with extreme fame – I’ve met plenty of A-listers who are dead behind the eyes. It’s not charm or extroversion either, nor beauty, and it’s not what we’d call “star quality” because it’s less showy than that. It’s almost indescribable, but “luminous” probably comes closest. I think it’s partly innate – God-given, Parton might have said – but it also comes from living with humility, gratitude and humour. Parton was luminous, and it wasn’t just the rhinestones. The cliche that you should never meet your heroes because you’ll only be disappointed only stands if you think famous people have somehow transcended the deep character flaws that make the rest of us human. Everyone has off days, or off years. Still, I’d been slightly dreading interviewing Parton. The machinery that surrounds a superstar interview – the holding rooms, the allotted time slots, the officious publicists – is designed to be intimidating, and it was all present on that autumn day in 2023. And then it was just Parton and me in a London hotel room, borderline uncomfortably close on a sofa, but unusually, no publicist sitting in, taking notes. Continue reading...

articles.title: Dolly Parton was a rare singer who proved herself to be an electric movie star
articles.snippet: From 9 to 5 to Steel Magnolias to Joyful Noise, the late star had real big screen presence that was impossible to imitate ‘I just give from my heart’: how Dolly Parton’s philanthropy focused most on helping children Celebrity tributes pour in for Dolly Parton: ‘a gift to the world’ There are an awful lot of singers who take a shot at movie stardom. Most of them start out playing singing ingenues and trail off a few movies later, after their limitations become clear, the novelty wears off or their interests wander back to music. Dolly Parton, who died on 25 August at the age of 80, had the barest outline of such a film career: She had a big hit out of the gate with 9 to 5, endured a sizable flop about a decade later with 1992’s Straight Talk signaling the end of her movie phase, and had a couple of minor postscripts in the years that followed – more cameos-as-herself than fully fleshed-out roles. (Presumably she was busy releasing over a dozen albums, making countless TV appearances, sending books to children, and funding vaccine research, among other endeavors.) Yet within a modest filmography consisting of just half a dozen leading roles in theatrical releases (and more than one widely regarded as a minor disaster), she showed more genuine screen presence than countless other multihyphenates. Maybe it helped that Parton introduced herself on screen in a non-musical role. Well, almost: 9 to 5, a 1980 workplace comedy where she starred alongside Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda, did yield a number one charting theme song, the Oscar-nominated tune of the same name. (The titular theme from Fame won, but which one still gets played on the radio more often?) The movie itself, where Parton plays an office secretary whose piggish boss (Dabney Coleman) lusts after her and whose co-workers (initially including Tomlin and Fonda) suspect, incorrectly, that she has given in to his desires, is a far more relatable comedy, sort of a neo-screwball-meets-women’s-picture with an additional early-‘80s feminist spin. articles.title: Affairs? Drugs? You could ask Dolly Parton about anything and get a laugh. Just stay away from politics …
articles.snippet: One autumn day in 2023 I bathed in the luminous glow of this utterly authentic star – and while she did have one weak spot, her life and music will speak for themselves Celebrity tributes pour in for Dolly Parton Dolly Parton’s 10 best deep cuts Alexis Petridis on Dolly Parton’s peerless career The great privilege of my kind of journalism is to get the chance to meet extraordinary people – some famous, many not – and very occasionally that person is beyond extraordinary. Dolly Parton, you may not be surprised to learn, was one of them. I’ve only come across it a handful of times. It has nothing to do with extreme fame – I’ve met plenty of A-listers who are dead behind the eyes. It’s not charm or extroversion either, nor beauty, and it’s not what we’d call “star quality” because it’s less showy than that. It’s almost indescribable, but “luminous” probably comes closest. I think it’s partly innate – God-given, Parton might have said – but it also comes from living with humility, gratitude and humour. Parton was luminous, and it wasn’t just the rhinestones. The cliche that you should never meet your heroes because you’ll only be disappointed only stands if you think famous people have somehow transcended the deep character flaws that make the rest of us human. Everyone has off days, or off years. Still, I’d been slightly dreading interviewing Parton. The machinery that surrounds a superstar interview – the holding rooms, the allotted time slots, the officious publicists – is designed to be intimidating, and it was all present on that autumn day in 2023. And then it was just Parton and me in a London hotel room, borderline uncomfortably close on a sofa, but unusually, no publicist sitting in, taking notes. Continue reading...

articles.title: Dolly Parton was a rare singer who proved herself to be an electric movie star
articles.snippet: From 9 to 5 to Steel Magnolias to Joyful Noise, the late star had real big screen presence that was impossible to imitate ‘I just give from my heart’: how Dolly Parton’s philanthropy focused most on helping children Celebrity tributes pour in for Dolly Parton: ‘a gift to the world’ There are an awful lot of singers who take a shot at movie stardom. Most of them start out playing singing ingenues and trail off a few movies later, after their limitations become clear, the novelty wears off or their interests wander back to music. Dolly Parton, who died on 25 August at the age of 80, had the barest outline of such a film career: She had a big hit out of the gate with 9 to 5, endured a sizable flop about a decade later with 1992’s Straight Talk signaling the end of her movie phase, and had a couple of minor postscripts in the years that followed – more cameos-as-herself than fully fleshed-out roles. (Presumably she was busy releasing over a dozen albums, making countless TV appearances, sending books to children, and funding vaccine research, among other endeavors.) Yet within a modest filmography consisting of just half a dozen leading roles in theatrical releases (and more than one widely regarded as a minor disaster), she showed more genuine screen presence than countless other multihyphenates. Maybe it helped that Parton introduced herself on screen in a non-musical role. Well, almost: 9 to 5, a 1980 workplace comedy where she starred alongside Lily Tomlin and Jane Fonda, did yield a number one charting theme song, the Oscar-nominated tune of the same name. (The titular theme from Fame won, but which one still gets played on the radio more often?) The movie itself, where Parton plays an office secretary whose piggish boss (Dabney Coleman) lusts after her and whose co-workers (initially including Tomlin and Fonda) suspect, incorrectly, that she has given in to his desires, is a far more relatable comedy, sort of a neo-screwball-meets-women’s-picture with an additional early-‘80s feminist spin.
